_doc: Engine input per player, keyed by players.json id. `ipa` is fed to BlueTTS verbatim (RenikudPlus IPA: ˈ before the stressed vowel, ʁ χ ʔ ts dʒ tʃ). It spells speak_he (the text inside a trailing parenthetical, else the full name). The same IPA is used in the name clip and inside the match clip, so the two always sound alike.

`g2p` is what RenikudPlus produced on its own for the bare speak_he (kept to show what was changed). `why` explains each change. `stt_variants` are spellings the STT check accepts as the same pronunciation; never add a spelling that implies a different sound. `stt_text` replaces speak_he as the STT target when the intended pronunciation is deliberately spelled differently from the card. Optional `ipa_match` is the same pronunciation nudged for the match clip only (e.g. a vowel length). Optional `speed` overrides the global pace for that player (BlueTTS divides duration by it). Optional `listen` is a judgement call worth checking by ear; tts/listen.html highlights it.
A player missing from this file falls back to RenikudPlus G2P of speak_he and is flagged in the QA report.

omri-glazer.why: G2P read עמרי as am-RI (om-RI in the match phrase); the name is OM-ri, with the colloquial first-syllable stress.

bruninho.why: The card shows ברונו רוברטו פריירה דה סילבה (ברוניניו); the voice reads only the parenthetical (HR3). Bruninho is bru-NI-nyo in Portuguese; G2P said bro-NI-nyo.

nigel-lonwijk.why: Dutch Lonwijk: LON-waik (Dutch w is between v and w). G2P said LON-vijk. With a plain v the STT wrote לונבייק / לומבייק (b) in 12/12 takes; with w it writes the club's own spelling לונווייק (8/12, A/B ab-r1).

jelle-bataille.why: Flemish Jelle Bataille: YE-le ba-TAI. G2P lost the first vowel (jla) and said be-TAI. Written plainly (jˈele) the STT heard יאללה / יא לבתי and 0/12 takes passed: 'yele' is not a Hebrew word and 'yalla' is. A long first vowel keeps the Flemish first-syllable stress and is heard as the club's own spelling יילה בתאי (8/12; the second model writes the same or ילד, i.e. YE-le(d)). ye-LE (jelˈe) passed more often (10/12) but moves the stress; kept as the fallback. Sport1 spells him ילה בטאי.
jelle-bataille.listen: YE-le ba-TAI with a slightly long first e; the STT kept hearing 'yalla' for a plain 'yele'. If it sounds odd, ye-LE (one-line change) is the robust fallback.

kenji-gorre.why: The club writes חורה (the Dutch g of Gorré), but Israeli media write קנג'י גורה (Sport1, Sport5, Walla) and pun on it as go-RE ("משהו טוב גורה", "גורה לכולם"), so fans and commentators say KEN-dji go-RE. The STT target is therefore גורה.
kenji-gorre.listen: Said go-RE, as the media and fans say it; the card (club spelling) reads חורה, kho-RE. A one-line change if he should sound like the card.

iyad-khalaili.why: G2P's i-YAD kha-LAI-li is right, but run together the initial i got lost: the second model heard יד ('yad') in 20/24 takes and the primary wrote יד in some match clips. A comma beat after the first name (as for Helio Varela in Tel Aviv) makes both models hear איאד in 10/12 takes (A/B ab-r2). אייד (consonantal yy, a unwritten, like אייל) and חלאילי / חליילי (one or two yods for the y glide) spell the same sounds; חלילי (no a) is rejected. In the match clip the a of the surname is lengthened (ipa_match): that version passes both STT models there (seed 8 of 12), while for the name clip the plain one is heard better.
iyad-khalaili.listen: A short beat between איאד and חלאיילי keeps the i of i-YAD audible; without it both STT models heard 'yad'.

tzunami.why: The card shows וונדרסון דה פריאטס סוארס (צונאמי); the voice reads only the parenthetical (HR3), his football name. G2P correct (tsu-NA-mi).

kenny-saief.why: G2P said k-NI (ka-NI in the match phrase); Kenny is KE-ni SAIF.

noam-shtaifman.why: G2P read the פ as p (SHTAIP-man); the club's English spelling is SHTAIFMAN.

yarin-levi.why: G2P correct (ya-RIN LE-vi, colloquial stress on Levi).

ali-mohamed.why: a-LI mu-KHA-mad: the Arabic and French stress of Ali, and the same a-LI the Tel Aviv game uses in מוחמד עלי קמארה. G2P said A-li.

pedrao.why: The card shows פדרו אוליביירה with no parenthetical, so the voice reads the full name (H4): Portuguese Oliveira, PED-ro o-li-VEI-ra. G2P said o-LIV-yra. Written plainly as -vˈejʁa the glide vanished before the r (STT: אוליברה, 0/12); giving it a vowel to ride on (-vˈejiʁa) brings back אוליביירה (8/12, A/B ab-r1).
pedrao.listen: Israeli media call him פדראו (Pedrão, the club's English name); the voice reads the displayed פדרו אוליביירה as H4 requires.

silva-kani.why: G2P stressed sil-VA (and said sil-BA in the match phrase); SIL-va KA-ni.

andrija-novakovich.why: an-DRI-ya no-va-KO-vich (the penultimate -ović stress Israelis use for Serbian names); a y glide instead of G2P's glottal stop. The STT writes the same sounds without the silent alefs.

pedro-barzao.why: Portuguese winger Pedro Brazão (the club's English page has BARZAO): PED-ro bra-ZAU, one diphthong instead of G2P's bra-ZA-'u.

adam-grimberg.why: G2P correct (a-DAM GRIM-berg). The STT writes the far commoner surname גרינברג for it: 47/48 takes across four spellings (plain, split גרים ברג, doubled m, long m; A/B ab-r1). In running Hebrew an n before b is usually said as m, so גרינברג and גרימברג sound all but identical and the variant is accepted.
adam-grimberg.listen: The STT always writes גרינברג (the common surname), never the card's גרימברג; before b the two sound nearly the same, so this is accepted. Worth one listen for a clear m.
